title: Outlook Automation: One Missed Rule
summary: Outlook automation failed for three days due to one misconfigured rule. Learn what went wrong and which safeguards prevent inbox breakdown.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Outlook automation free?


Rules cost nothing extra: they ship with Outlook itself. Power Automate flows that use standard connectors are generally covered by an existing Microsoft 365 subscription, while premium connectors need a separate paid license.


Check which connector tier a flow touches before you build it, because a flow that silently depends on a premium connector becomes a licensing problem later.


### Can Outlook rules run when the app is closed?


It depends on the rule type. Rules that run on the server, such as moving mail to a folder or forwarding it, keep working with Outlook closed. Rules Microsoft marks as client-only, such as playing a sound or printing, need the desktop app open.


If a rule matters, make it server-side, or move the job into a flow that runs in the cloud.


### Do I need Power Automate or can I use another tool?


You need Power Automate only when the job crosses Microsoft's boundary or needs steps a rule can't express. Rules cover sorting, flagging and forwarding inside the mailbox. For anything touching another app, a third-party automation tool can do the same work.


The test is the same either way: does it have an owner, a cap and a failure alert? A tool that fails with no alert just moves the mess somewhere else.


### Can automation read emails with AI safely?


Safely enough, if you limit what the AI step can do. Email bodies are untrusted input, so a message can contain instructions aimed at your model.


Let the AI step classify or summarize, and keep sending, deleting and forwarding behind a fixed rule or a human approval.


Also check what your organization's policy says about sending mail content to an external model before you wire one in.


### How do I stop an automation failing silently?


Make failure produce a message somebody sees. Send an alert to a team channel, not a personal inbox, whenever a run errors.


Add a heartbeat as well: a periodic check that confirms the flow ran at all, because a disabled or expired connection throws no error.


Name one person as owner, so the alert has somewhere to land. The failures that hurt are the ones where nothing happened and nothing said so.
